steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your chest.
Angle the hands so the fingertips meet above the middle.
Touch the fingertips together to form the shape of a roof.
Keep the fingertips joined briefly, then gently release the shape.
Hold your arms steady with a calm, settled expression throughout.
tip: Plural of “Home” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Open both hands in front of your body at chest height.
Touch the tip of each index finger to the tip of its thumb.
Hold both rounded shapes up, palms facing down and out.
Move the hands side to side in small, smooth arcs.
Keep the arcs gentle and rhythmic, as if conducting an orchestra.
tip: Plural of “Music” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Extend the index and middle fingers of your dominant hand together.
Press the tips of the two fingers lightly against your forehead.
Twist the hand forwards at the wrist in one smooth turn.
Finish with the fingertips pointing forwards, in front of your face.
Keep the elbow relaxed and mouth the word 'name' as you twist.
tip: Plural of “Name” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of your chest, palm facing up.
Place your dominant flat hand just above it, palm facing down, fingers together.
Sweep the dominant hand up and back over your shoulder in one smooth arc.
Keep the palm facing down the whole way, as if brushing the past behind you.
tip: Plural of “History” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Make a fist with each hand and extend only your pinky fingers straight up.
Raise both hands to your temples, pinky tips beside your head, palms facing each other.
Move both hands down and together in front of your chest until the pinky tips meet.
Hold the pinky tips touching briefly at the centre, palms still facing each other.
tip: Plural of “College” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Form an L with your dominant hand: index finger pointing straight up, thumb sticking out sideways.
Curl your remaining fingers into your palm, keeping the palm facing forward.
Raise the hand from your chest to beside your eye, fingertip aimed upward.
Hold it briefly by your eye, then lower it back to your chest.
tip: “Tests” is signed with the base TEST sign.

steps: Form an L with your dominant hand: index finger pointing straight up, thumb sticking out sideways.
Curl your remaining fingers into your palm, keeping the palm facing forward.
Raise the hand from your chest to beside your eye, fingertip aimed upward.
Hold it briefly by your eye, then lower it back to your chest.
tip: “Testing” is signed with the base TEST sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Form an L with your dominant hand: index finger pointing straight up, thumb sticking out sideways.
Curl your remaining fingers into your palm, keeping the palm facing forward.
Raise the hand from your chest to beside your eye, fingertip aimed upward.
Hold it briefly by your eye, then lower it back to your chest.
tip: Past form of “Test” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your dominant hand up in front of your chin with only the index finger extended upright.
Curl your other fingers down and rest your thumb across them, palm facing you.
Bend just the index fingertip down in one quick tap, like a tiny hook.
Keep the hand still in front of your chin while only the fingertip moves.
tip: Plural of “Word” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Make a loose fist with your non-dominant hand and point the thumb straight up.
Hold that thumb-up fist steady in front of your chest.
Raise your dominant index finger above the thumb, palm facing inward toward you.
Bring the fingertip straight down to touch the tip of the upright thumb.
tip: Plural of “Answer” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold your open dominant hand up beside your cheek, fingers spread wide.
Face your palm forward, away from your face, at cheek height.
Flutter all your fingers repeatedly with small quick bends, like shimmering.
Keep the hand still beside your face while only the fingers move.
tip: Plural of “Color” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Make a fist with your dominant hand and stick your thumb straight up, holding it in front of your chest.
Hold your other hand in a relaxed fist beside it, about a fist-width away.
Twist your wrist sharply so the thumb flicks from pointing up to pointing across toward your other fist.
Keep your palm facing inward toward the other hand throughout the flick.
tip: “Buys” is signed with the base BUY sign.

steps: Make a fist with each hand and stick both thumbs straight up, palms facing each other.
Hold both fists in front of your chest, about shoulder-width apart.
Bring the fists slightly toward each other while twisting both wrists to flick the thumbs outward.
Finish with both thumbs pointing out to the sides and hold for a beat.
tip: “Sells” is signed with the base SELL sign.

steps: Make a fist with each hand and stick both thumbs straight up, palms facing each other.
Hold both fists in front of your chest, about shoulder-width apart.
Bring the fists slightly toward each other while twisting both wrists to flick the thumbs outward.
Finish with both thumbs pointing out to the sides and hold for a beat.
tip: “Selling” is signed with the base SELL sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Make a fist with each hand and stick both thumbs straight up.
Hold both thumb-up fists in front of your chest, palms facing each other.
Push your dominant fist forward, away from your body, thumb still pointing up.
Keep the other fist steady at your chest as a starting point for the journey.
tip: “Travels” is signed with the base TRAVEL sign.

steps: Hold your dominant hand out in front of you with the fingers curved, like a claw.
Keep your palm facing inward toward your own body, fingers still curved.
Close your fingers into a tight fist, as if grabbing something from the air.
Pull the fist back to touch your chest in one smooth motion.
tip: “Gets” is signed with the base GET sign.

steps: Hold your dominant hand out in front of you with the fingers curved, like a claw.
Keep your palm facing inward toward your own body, fingers still curved.
Close your fingers into a tight fist, as if grabbing something from the air.
Pull the fist back to touch your chest in one smooth motion.
tip: “Getting” is signed with the base GET sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Hold your dominant hand up beside your eye with only the index finger extended upward.
Keep your palm facing inward toward you, fingertip pointing at the sky.
Sweep the hand downward in front of your body while curling your fingers closed.
Finish in a tight fist at chest height, as if you have grabbed what you were seeking.
tip: “Finds” is signed with the base FIND sign.

steps: Hold your dominant hand up beside your eye with only the index finger extended upward.
Keep your palm facing inward toward you, fingertip pointing at the sky.
Sweep the hand downward in front of your body while curling your fingers closed.
Finish in a tight fist at chest height, as if you have grabbed what you were seeking.
tip: “Finding” is signed with the base FIND sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Pinch the thumb and fingertips of each hand together, as if holding something tiny.
Raise both pinched hands from your waist to the centre of your chest, palms facing each other.
Touch the pinched fingertips of both hands together in the middle.
Give both wrists a small twist against each other, like moulding clay.
tip: “Makes” is signed with the base MAKE sign.

steps: Pinch the thumb and fingertips of each hand together, as if holding something tiny.
Raise both pinched hands from your waist to the centre of your chest, palms facing each other.
Touch the pinched fingertips of both hands together in the middle.
Give both wrists a small twist against each other, like moulding clay.
tip: “Making” is signed with the base MAKE sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Hold both hands flat with fingers together, stacking your dominant hand on top of the other at waist level.
Raise both hands to chest height while separating them outward, keeping the palms facing down as they move.
Rotate your wrists so the palms turn to face each other, finishing with both flat hands held apart at chest level.
tip: “Opens” is signed with the base OPEN sign.

steps: Make a 'Y' with your dominant hand by extending the thumb and little finger while folding the middle fingers down.
Raise the Y hand to the side of your face, bringing the thumb up beside your mouth with the palm facing you.
Hold the handshape briefly at your cheek, then lower your hand back to a neutral resting position.
tip: “Calls” is signed with the base CALL sign.

steps: Make a 'Y' with your dominant hand by extending the thumb and little finger while folding the middle fingers down.
Raise the Y hand to the side of your face, bringing the thumb up beside your mouth with the palm facing you.
Hold the handshape briefly at your cheek, then lower your hand back to a neutral resting position.
tip: Past form of “Call” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand, folding the remaining fingers into a loose fist.
Touch your chin with the fingertip, keeping the finger pointing upward and the palm facing down.
Flick your hand forward away from your chin so the finger points ahead at chest height.
tip: “Says” is signed with the base SAY sign.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you at waist level with the palm facing up.
Curve the fingers of your dominant hand into a rounded cupped shape, as if holding a coin.
Bring the cupped hand down from above and tap your fingertips once onto the open palm.
tip: “Pays” is signed with the base PAY sign.

steps: Hold both hands flat with fingers together in front of your chest, palms facing down.
Move your hands toward each other until your dominant hand comes down to rest on top of the other.
Press the stacked hands down slightly, like closing a lid, then hold them together briefly.
tip: “Closes” is signed with the base CLOSE sign.

steps: Hold both hands flat with fingers together in front of your chest, palms facing down.
Move your hands toward each other until your dominant hand comes down to rest on top of the other.
Press the stacked hands down slightly, like closing a lid, then hold them together briefly.
tip: Past form of “Close” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Raise your dominant hand toward the side of your head with the fingers open and relaxed.
Close your hand into a fist as it reaches your forehead, tapping the knuckles firmly against it.
Keep the back of the fist facing outward with the palm turned toward you as it touches.
tip: “Remembers” is signed with the base REMEMBER sign.

steps: Hold both flat hands in front of your chest with fingers together and palms facing down.
Lift one hand up and place it flat on top of the other, like laying a brick.
Alternate hands, stacking each one on top of the last to build upward layer by layer.
tip: “Builds” is signed with the base BUILD sign.

steps: Hold your dominant hand open in front of your chest, fingers extended and pointing upward, palm facing forward.
Raise your hand in a smooth motion from chest level to just below your chin.
Curl your fingers into a firm fist as your hand rises, ending with your knuckles facing forward.
Keep your other hand relaxed and still at your side throughout the sign.
tip: “Wins” is signed with the base WIN sign.

steps: Make a firm fist with your dominant hand, wrapping your thumb across your fingers.
Raise the fist to the middle of your chest, holding it a short distance in front of your body.
Turn your wrist so the back of your hand faces forward, with your knuckles pointing away from you.
Hold the fist still in that position for a moment, keeping your other hand relaxed at your side.
tip: “Holds” is signed with the base HOLD sign.

steps: Form a V with each hand by extending your index and middle fingers, keeping the other fingers curled.
Hold both V hands in front of your upper chest, fingers pointing upward, palms facing each other.
Swing both hands down toward your waist, rotating your wrists so the V fingers point downward.
Swing your hands back up to chest height, rotating so the V fingers point upward again.
Repeat the up-and-down swing, letting the two Vs bounce together like dancing legs.
tip: “Dances” is signed with the base DANCE sign.

steps: Form a V with each hand by extending your index and middle fingers, keeping the other fingers curled.
Hold both V hands in front of your upper chest, fingers pointing upward, palms facing each other.
Swing both hands down toward your waist, rotating your wrists so the V fingers point downward.
Swing your hands back up to chest height, rotating so the V fingers point upward again.
Repeat the up-and-down swing, letting the two Vs bounce together like dancing legs.
tip: “Dancing” is signed with the base DANCE sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Form a V with each hand by extending your index and middle fingers, keeping the other fingers curled.
Hold both V hands in front of your upper chest, fingers pointing upward, palms facing each other.
Swing both hands down toward your waist, rotating your wrists so the V fingers point downward.
Swing your hands back up to chest height, rotating so the V fingers point upward again.
Repeat the up-and-down swing, letting the two Vs bounce together like dancing legs.
tip: Past form of “Dance” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of your waist, palm facing upward like a small platform.
Form a V with your dominant hand by extending your index and middle fingers, keeping the rest curled.
Point the two V fingers straight down above your upturned palm, with the back of your hand facing forward.
Lower the V fingertips onto your palm so the two fingers stand upright on it, then hold briefly.
tip: “Standing” is signed with the base STAND sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Make loose fists with both hands, as if gripping a cloth in each hand, palms facing forward.
Hold both fists in front of your torso, between chest and waist height.
Scrub the fists up and down alternately, raising one fist as the other lowers.
Repeat the alternating polishing motion, like buffing a surface until it shines.
tip: “Cleans” is signed with the base CLEAN sign.

steps: Make loose fists with both hands, as if gripping a cloth in each hand, palms facing forward.
Hold both fists in front of your torso, between chest and waist height.
Scrub the fists up and down alternately, raising one fist as the other lowers.
Repeat the alternating polishing motion, like buffing a surface until it shines.
tip: “Cleaning” is signed with the base CLEAN sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Make loose fists with both hands, as if gripping a cloth in each hand, palms facing forward.
Hold both fists in front of your torso, between chest and waist height.
Scrub the fists up and down alternately, raising one fist as the other lowers.
Repeat the alternating polishing motion, like buffing a surface until it shines.
tip: Past form of “Clean” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand up in front of your chest, fingers extended together.
Point your dominant index finger downward, curling your other fingers into your palm.
Tap the tip of your index finger once onto the back of your other hand near the wrist.
Keep the tap light and brief, like pointing at an imaginary watch on your wrist.
tip: Plural of “Month” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Bend the fingers of both hands into loose claws, as if holding a small ball in each hand.
Hold both hands in front of your waist, palms facing downward, a short distance apart.
Move both hands forward together in a winding, snake-like path, swaying gently side to side.
Keep the claw shapes steady as your hands meander forward like a winding river.
tip: Plural of “River” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold both hands flat in front of your chest, fingers extended and slightly spread, palms facing down.
Start with your hands close together at the center of your chest.
Sweep both hands outward to your sides in a smooth, wavy motion, like rolling waves.
Finish with your arms extended wide, palms still facing down toward the water surface.
tip: Plural of “Sea” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold both hands open in front of your waist, fingers extended together, palms facing inward.
Start with your hands low and wide apart, like the broad base of a mountain.
Raise both hands diagonally upward and inward, tracing the two slopes of the mountain.
Touch your fingertips together at chest height to form the pointed peak, then hold.
tip: Plural of “Mountain” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Bring your fingertips and thumb together into a bunched shape.
Tap the bunched fingers against your mouth twice.
tip: Past form of “Eat” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Bend the index finger of your dominant hand into a hook.
Start with the hand in front of your body.
Pull the bent finger toward yourself, like beckoning.
tip: Past form of “Come” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Pinch the thumb and fingertips of each hand together, as if holding something tiny.
Raise both pinched hands from your waist to the centre of your chest, palms facing each other.
Touch the pinched fingertips of both hands together in the middle.
Give both wrists a small twist against each other, like moulding clay.
tip: Past form of “Make” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand, folding the remaining fingers into a loose fist.
Touch your chin with the fingertip, keeping the finger pointing upward and the palm facing down.
Flick your hand forward away from your chin so the finger points ahead at chest height.
tip: Past form of “Say” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your dominant hand out in front of you with the fingers curved, like a claw.
Keep your palm facing inward toward your own body, fingers still curved.
Close your fingers into a tight fist, as if grabbing something from the air.
Pull the fist back to touch your chest in one smooth motion.
tip: Past form of “Get” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Make a fist with your thumb sticking out.
Tap the side of your head with your thumb, repeating the tap.
tip: Past form of “Know” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand, folding the others away.
Raise the fingertip to the side of your forehead, near the temple.
Tap the side of your head once or twice with the fingertip.
Keep your palm facing inward and the finger pointing at the head.
Hold a thoughtful expression — the sign needs the 'thinking' face to land.
tip: Past form of “Think” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your torso, fingers together.
Touch the middle fingertips of both hands lightly against your chest.
Drag both hands slowly upward across your chest without lifting them away.
Keep your palms facing inward toward your body for the whole movement.
Mirror the feeling with your face — soft and open for good feelings, tense for bad ones.
tip: Past form of “Feel” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Make a fist with your dominant hand and stick your thumb straight up, holding it in front of your chest.
Hold your other hand in a relaxed fist beside it, about a fist-width away.
Twist your wrist sharply so the thumb flicks from pointing up to pointing across toward your other fist.
Keep your palm facing inward toward the other hand throughout the flick.
tip: Past form of “Buy” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing up like paper.
Pinch your dominant index fingertip against your thumb, as if holding a pen.
Make small side-to-side scribbling motions across the open palm surface.
Keep your dominant palm angled sideways and the strokes quick and light.
Keep the writing hand moving — a still pen on a palm reads as pointing.
tip: Past form of “Write” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Make an open pinched handshape with your dominant hand, thumb and fingertips held apart.
Start the hand a short distance in front of your chest, palm roughly facing sideways.
Pull the hand back toward your chest in one decisive motion while closing the pinch shut.
Keep the movement single and firm, like plucking one option out of the air.
Pair it with a decided expression and mouth 'choose' as your hand closes.
tip: Past form of “Choose” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Curve your dominant hand into a loose C shape, as if holding a cup.
Lift the hand up to your mouth.
Tip your wrist toward your face, as though taking a drink from the cup.
tip: Past form of “Drink” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Close both hands into tight fists, keeping the thumbs tucked inside.
Hold both fists in front of your chest at shoulder width.
Pump the fists up and down in quick alternation, like pumping arms while running.
Keep the fists vertical, moving about a hand's length with each pump.
Lean your body slightly forward — the lean sells the running motion.
tip: Past form of “Run” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your dominant hand open in front of your chest, fingers extended and pointing upward, palm facing forward.
Raise your hand in a smooth motion from chest level to just below your chin.
Curl your fingers into a firm fist as your hand rises, ending with your knuckles facing forward.
Keep your other hand relaxed and still at your side throughout the sign.
tip: Past form of “Win” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your dominant hand up beside your eye with only the index finger extended upward.
Keep your palm facing inward toward you, fingertip pointing at the sky.
Sweep the hand downward in front of your body while curling your fingers closed.
Finish in a tight fist at chest height, as if you have grabbed what you were seeking.
tip: Past form of “Find” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Make a firm fist with your dominant hand, wrapping your thumb across your fingers.
Raise the fist to the middle of your chest, holding it a short distance in front of your body.
Turn your wrist so the back of your hand faces forward, with your knuckles pointing away from you.
Hold the fist still in that position for a moment, keeping your other hand relaxed at your side.
tip: Past form of “Hold” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you at waist level with the palm facing up.
Curve the fingers of your dominant hand into a rounded cupped shape, as if holding a coin.
Bring the cupped hand down from above and tap your fingertips once onto the open palm.
tip: Past form of “Pay” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of your waist, palm facing upward like a small platform.
Form a V with your dominant hand by extending your index and middle fingers, keeping the rest curled.
Point the two V fingers straight down above your upturned palm, with the back of your hand facing forward.
Lower the V fingertips onto your palm so the two fingers stand upright on it, then hold briefly.
tip: Past form of “Stand” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold both flat hands in front of your chest with fingers together and palms facing down.
Lift one hand up and place it flat on top of the other, like laying a brick.
Alternate hands, stacking each one on top of the last to build upward layer by layer.
tip: Past form of “Build” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.
